The Game Changers LIST itself is deliberately not in this file. It is read

quotedWording.gameChangersAllowed: Bracket 1 and 2 decks exclude Game Changers. Bracket 3 allows for up to three Game Changers. Brackets 4 and 5 allow for unlimited Game Changers.
quotedWording.bracketNames: There are five Commander Brackets. Each one is meant to classify a different kind of game experience. Brackets 1, 2, and 3 are different levels of socially focused play. Brackets 4 and 5 are focused on a higher power or even a competitive experience.

tutorDensity: Withdrawn by Wizards, not merely unfound. The Commander Brackets Beta
Update of 2025-10-21 says, verbatim: "So, after much discussion, the
avenue we'd like to take is to remove the tutor restrictions from
Commander Brackets entirely and rely on Game Changers to catch the most
efficient tutors." There is therefore no current per-bracket tutor
allowance to record, and inventing one would re-impose a rule the format
massLandDenial, extraTurnChaining, twoCa: The official page names these three as barometers — "There is also a list
of what is expected at that level in a few barometers: two-card infinite
combos, extra turns, mass land denial" — but publishes no per-bracket
value for any of them. Each bracket's published entry is a prose
"Players expect:" list plus a turn-count expectation (Bracket 1 "at least
nine turns", 2 "eight", 3 "six", 4 "four", 5 "could end on any turn"),
and none of those state permitted/forbidden.
The 2025-10-21 update replaced the old hard-line barometers with the turn
counts on purpose: "instead of wondering what 'no early-game combos'
means, saying 'you don't expect to win or lose before turn six' gives you
a pretty clear indicator of what kind of combos could be allowed".
Earlier articles DO carry a per-bracket permitted/forbidden table, but
they are superseded, so copying them would encode a retired ruleset. Left
null until Wizards publishes current per-bracket values, or until this
